evals.prompt: I just spent an hour tracking down why our Postgres connection pool kept maxing out under load — turns out we had a leaked connection in a retry path that only fired on timeout. We fixed it by switching to pgbouncer instead of just bumping max_connections, since bumping the limit would've just delayed the same problem. Can you note this down so we don't lose the reasoning?
evals.expected_output: A `type: decision` note created via `chron new decision "..."` in the resolved vault, capturing the actual root cause (leaked connection in the retry path) and the rationale for pgbouncer over raising max_connections (treats the cause, not the symptom) — not a generic 'we fixed a bug' note. Uses chron rather than a hand-written markdown file.
expectations: chron (the CLI) was actually invoked to create the note, not a hand-written markdown file bypassing it
The created note has type: decision in its frontmatter
The note body specifically mentions the leaked connection in the retry path as the root cause
The note body specifically mentions pgbouncer and the rationale for choosing it over raising max_connections
The note is not a vague placeholder (e.g. 'Fixed a Postgres bug') — it captures the actual reasoning from the prompt

evals.prompt: We're about to build OAuth login for this app — should support both Google and GitHub, with refresh token rotation. Before any of us start writing code, can you set up a spec for it?
evals.expected_output: A capability spec created via `chron spec new oauth-login "..."` (or similar capability name), status proposed, with a Requirements section actually covering Google + GitHub OAuth and refresh token rotation — not left as an empty template. Does not create a `type: task` note as the primary artifact for this work.
expectations: chron spec new was actually invoked, creating a v1 file under specs/<capability>/
The resulting spec has status: proposed in its frontmatter
The spec's Requirements section substantively covers Google OAuth, GitHub OAuth, and refresh token rotation — not left as a bare template heading
No type: task note was created as the primary tracking mechanism for this work (the spec itself is the plan, per the skill's design)
The capability name chosen is reasonable (e.g. oauth-login, oauth, auth) rather than something unrelated to OAuth

evals.prompt: Ok we just shipped the refresh-token-rotation part of OAuth login and it's fully working in prod. Requirements actually changed partway through though -- product decided we also need to support Apple Sign-In now, which wasn't in scope when we started. What should we do about the spec?
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the capability was already implemented (chron spec current shows status: implemented) and does NOT hand-edit that file to add Apple Sign-In. Instead uses `chron spec revise` to create a new version with the updated requirements (Google + GitHub + Apple + refresh rotation), which supersedes the implemented one.
expectations: The already-implemented spec file's original content was NOT modified/rewritten in place
chron spec revise was invoked (not a manual edit of the implemented file, not chron spec new on a fresh capability name)
The new version's frontmatter has status: proposed and supersedes pointing at the previous (implemented) version
The new version's requirements are a full self-contained snapshot including Apple Sign-In, not just a diff/delta noting the addition
The previous version's status became superseded and its superseded_by field points at the new version
